answer: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common type of skin cancer.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) is the most common subtype of thyroid cancer.
MGZL is most commonly seen in those between 20 to 40 years of age.
Endocrine therapy is used for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer; HER2-negative status influences targeted therapy choices. (Context does not explicitly name CDK4/6 inhibitors.)
Diagnostic methods for bone sarcomas include imaging tests (PET/CT, PET/MRI, bone scan) and biopsy.
Long-term HPV infection is the strongest risk factor for cervical cancer; weakened immune system also increases risk.
Popcorn-shaped cells distinguish NLPHL from CHL (which is known for Reed-Sternberg cells).
Breast cancer commonly metastasizes to the bone (also lungs, liver, brain, distant lymph nodes).
Lung cancer screening is recommended for people at high risk for lung cancer.
Classic Hodgkin lymphoma (CHL) is most frequently associated with Reed-Sternberg cells.
After CSCC treatment, regular skin and lymph node exams are recommended; for local CSCC monitoring is most important during the first 2 years, then once a year for life.
Primary CNS lymphoma can relapse in the brain (and other CNS sites such as spinal cord and eyes).
Mediastinal gray zone lymphoma (MGZL) has overlapping features with primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma (PMBL) and Hodgkin lymphoma.
Biomarker testing is essential to diagnose follicular lymphoma (FL); BCL2 is a known FL biomarker. (Context names FL biomarker testing without specifying BCL2.)
MGZL is usually treated with chemotherapy.
Siewert types describe where the tumor is relative to the esophagus and stomach; used for staging tumors at the esophagogastric junction.
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (PD-1 inhibitors such as nivolumab/cemiplimab/pembrolizumab) are preferred for metastatic CSCC.
Blood tests for initial colon cancer evaluation include complete blood count (CBC) and chemistry profile (also CEA).
Primary CNS lymphoma can involve the spinal cord, cerebrospinal fluid, and eyes.
Tis is carcinoma in situ — an intraductal tumor confined to the epithelium.
Treatment of CLL/SLL is the same because the cancer cells are the same; options include oral medications, IV infusions, and combination therapies.
Symptoms that may indicate throat cancer include difficulty swallowing, sore throat, and changes in voice.
Pathologic stage in throat cancer is determined by examining tissue removed during surgery.
Throat squamous cell carcinoma is associated with HPV-mediated, p16-positive, and p16-negative genetic alterations.
Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer is typically treated with platinum-based chemotherapy (often combined with bevacizumab/maintenance therapy).
Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma (CBCL) starts specifically in B cells.
IDH mutation is a key biomarker used to classify gliomas.
Treatment planning for mouth cancer is based on tumor location and stage.
Yes — family history of colorectal cancer is a known risk factor for colon cancer.
Clinical trials are the preferred treatment approach for subtypes such as BCR::ABL1-negative or BCR::ABL1-like B-ALL.
